title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — Pricing and Splitting a Coinsurance Block
content:
**Rule in force.** Each booked days 21 through 100 block is priced at the daily coinsurance rate of the calendar year in which those days of service fall, never at the rate of the posting date or of the admission year; a block that spans two years is booked as separate service months and priced month by month. The block total is the day count times that rate. The total is split by the tier's coinsurance shares: the resident amount is the block total times the resident share percent, rounded half up to the cent, and the secondary amount is the block total minus the resident amount, billed to the tier's secondary liable party; one charge row is posted per liable party with a non-zero amount, and a zero amount is not posted. Days 1 through the full-coverage day limit carry no coinsurance and are never charged. A block is charged once per liable party, apart from a rebill of a denied secondary share.

**Retired clause — no longer in force.** The following sentence of this Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage rule is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for blocks of coinsurance days: "The tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split." The rest of this rule remains in force.

### The split per tier

Each tier's resident share percent, secondary share percent and secondary liable party are the tier's own figures in the cost-sharing split schedule; this rule applies them as stated above, with the rate of the year of service and half-up rounding of the resident amount to the cent.

**Duplicate test.** A block is charged once per liable party, read from the system record of charges naming the booked-days entry and that party; a rebill of a denied secondary share is the one exception.

*Hypothetical worked example (QMB Medicaid Crossover tier, 13 coinsurance days furnished in 2026):* the block total is 13 times 217.00, that is 2821.00. The resident amount is 2821.00 times 0 percent, that is 0.00, and is not posted; the secondary amount is 2821.00 less 0.00, that is 2821.00, billed to the state Medicaid crossover. One charge row is posted.

superseded_clauses: The tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split.
